title: A formal isomorphism gives an affine etale span over the completed base
statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}D$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and let $X\to S$ and $Y\to T$ be finite type morphisms with $X,Y$ affine [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix $x\mapsto s$ and $y\mapsto t$, put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, and put $B=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$, where completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $\sigma:\mathcal O_{T,t}\to\widehat A$ be a local ring homomorphism, meaning that it sends the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal. Write $b$ for the closed point of $B$, $\lambda:B\to T$ for the induced map, $X_B=X\times_SB$, and $Y_B=Y\times_{T,\lambda}B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $y_B\in Y_B$ maps to $(y,b)$ and there is an isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y_B,y_B}$ of $\widehat A$-algebras. Then $B$ is Noetherian and $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(b)$ is an isomorphism [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-residue-field]. There is a unique point $x_B\in X_B$ above $(x,b)$, with $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(x_B)$ an isomorphism. There exist an affine scheme $H$ of finite presentation over $B$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a point $h\in H$ over $b$, and étale $B$-morphisms $a:H\to X_B$ and $c:H\to Y_B$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] with $a(h)=x_B$ and $c(h)=y_B$, such that the induced maps $\kappa(x_B)\to\kappa(h)$ and $\kappa(y_B)\to\kappa(h)$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, first proof paragraph and affine reduction; Tag 0CAV, lemma-isomorphism-approximation, with an affine finite-presentation neighbourhood of the marked point.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $S$ is Noetherian. Since $S$ is affine, [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] makes $R$ Noetherian. The stalk description [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $A$ with the localization of $R$ at the prime of $s$; hence [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $A$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; Properties Tag 01OW, lemma-locally-Noetherian; Algebra Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence

proof.text: Write $C=\widehat A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $C$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] it is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A C$, and the canonical map identifies $\kappa(s)$ with $\kappa(b)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] with $M=A$ and $I=\mathfrak m_A$, which is finitely generated since $A$ is Noetherian. This makes $C$ complete at $\mathfrak m_A C$: its powers are $\mathfrak m_A^n C$, so its ring-adic and the cited module-adic filtrations coincide. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-g-ring] makes $C$ a G-ring. The one affine open $B=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is a Noetherian affine covering, so $B$ is locally Noetherian; any open cover has a member containing $b$, which contains a principal open $D(f)$ with $f\notin\mathfrak m_C$. Such $f$ is a unit, so $D(f)=B$. Thus this member alone covers $B$, proving quasi-compactness and hence Noetherianity.

Apply [lem-trf-completed-local-base-change] to $X\to S$ at $x$. This supplies the unique $x_B$ over $(x,b)$ and a canonical $C$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X_B,x_B}$. To check the residue clause, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] describes this fibre by the primes of $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(b)$. Under the canonical residue isomorphism in step 2 this tensor product is $\kappa(x)$ via $r\otimes v\mapsto r\,\iota(v)$, where $\iota:\kappa(b)\cong\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$. It is a field, whose only prime is zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] its residue field identifies with $\kappa(x_B)$ compatibly with $\kappa(x)$; therefore the canonical map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(x_B)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, first proof paragraph; Schemes Tag 01JT, lemma-points-fibre-product

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $X_B\to B$ and $Y_B\to B$ are of finite type. Let $\psi:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y_B,y_B}$ be the given $C$-algebra isomorphism. The composite $\theta\psi^{-1}:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y_B,y_B}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X_B,x_B}$ is a $C$-algebra isomorphism, hence an $\mathcal O_{B,b}$-algebra isomorphism: $C$ is local, so $\mathcal O_{B,b}=C$. Both marked points lie over $b$, and step 2 verifies that this base stalk is a G-ring. Apply [lem-trf-isomorphism-completion-approximation] over $B$ with $N=2$. It gives $(X_B,x_B)\leftarrow(U,u)\to(Y_B,y_B)$ over $B$, both arrows étale and both residue maps isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0CAV, lemma-isomorphism-approximation, applied as in Tag 0GDX, first proof paragraph

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] for $U\to X_B$, the canonical residue point $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$, and the open $U$ itself. Obtain an affine open neighbourhood $j:H\hookrightarrow U$ and its point $h$ over $u$. Its composite $a:H\to X_B$ is étale. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], $c:H\to U\to Y_B$ is also étale. An open restriction has the same local ring at its marked point (sections on neighbourhoods contained in the open are cofinal in the stalk colimit), so $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(h)$ is an isomorphism. Thus both required residue maps remain isomorphisms. The arrows remain over $B$ and $h$ maps to $b$.

source.place: Schemes Tag 01HR, section-affine-schemes (affine open neighbourhoods); Morphisms Tags 02GP, lemma-open-immersion-etale and 02GN, lemma-composition-etale

proof.text: The étale arrow $a$ is locally of finite type by the definition [def-weil-etale-morphism] and its unramified clause [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Its composite $H\to X_B\to B$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Since $B$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes this composite locally of finite presentation. Since $B$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] applied to its structure map makes $B$ separated. Since $H$ is affine and $B$ separated, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-separated-target-affine-morphism] makes $H\to B$ affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Together these are exactly the finite-presentation conditions required in the statement.
